question: What percentage of tests will be positive for rhinovirus/enterovirus in the United States for the week ending October 24, 2026, in CDC data?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the percent of tests positive for rhinovirus/enterovirus in the United States for the week ending 2026-10-24 in CDC's the National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System (NREVSS) percent positivity data (data.cdc.gov dataset rgnm-fkqb), as posted on 2026-10-30.
research:
# Research brief: US rhinovirus/enterovirus (RV/EV) test positivity, week ending 2026-10-24

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on CDC NREVSS dataset rgnm-fkqb on data.cdc.gov, using the row with level "National", pathogen "RV/EV" and week ending 2026-10-24, in the version posted 2026-10-30. The dataset has these fields: mmwrweek_end, tests, detections, percent_pos and posted. [data.cdc.gov API](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)
- The dataset seems to keep only the most recent posting. When I asked for rows posted on or before 2026-09-14, it returned nothing, so I could not get the exact version that existed on 2026-09-14. The figures below come from the dataset as it can be accessed now, cut off at weeks that would have been published by 2026-09-14. Later postings may have revised earlier weeks slightly.
- Latest weeks that would have been available around 2026-09-14 (national RV/EV positivity):
  - 2026-09-05: 28.07% (16,874 tests). [data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)
  - 2026-08-29: 24.83%
  - 2026-08-22: 21.03%
  - 2026-08-15: 16.94%
  - 2026-08-08: 14.70%
  - Summer low: 13.75% (2026-07-18)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing that settles the question had happened by 2026-09-14. The late-summer RV/EV rise, tied to schools reopening, was well underway, with positivity up about 13 points from mid-July to early September. In earlier years, positivity peaked in mid-to-late September or early October and then fell slowly through late October.

## 3. Recent news
- I did not search news sources separately. The CDC data show the 2026 back-to-school rise starting in mid-August, about the same time as in 2024 and 2025. [data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)
- Earlier in the year there was an unusually high spring hump, peaking at 26.07% for the week ending 2026-05-09. In 2025 the comparable peak was about 22.5%.

## 4. Base rates
All values below are national RV/EV percent positive from the same dataset. [data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)

| Year | Early September | Peak (week ending) | Comparable week in late October |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2021 | 24.21 (9/04) | 27.82 (10/09) | 25.93 (10/23) |
| 2022 | 31.73 (9/03) | 32.46 (9/24) | 24.72 (10/22) |
| 2023 | 27.40 (9/02) | 29.61 (9/23) | 24.51 (10/21) |
| 2024 | 25.84 (9/07) | 30.63 (9/21) | 25.82 (10/26) |
| 2025 | 29.51 (9/06) | 30.66 (9/20) | 24.58 (10/25) |
| 2026 | 28.07 (9/05) | ? | ? |

- **Late-October values, 2021 to 2025:** 24.5% to 25.9%, average about 25.1%. The spread across years is small, about 1.4 points, even though peaks varied from about 27.8% to 32.5%.
- **Typical path:** a peak of 29% to 32% around the third or fourth week of September, then a decline of about 1 point per week to 24% to 26% by late October.
- **How 2026 compares:** early-September positivity (28.07%) is roughly in line with 2023 and 2025 and higher than 2021 and 2024. Weekly tests (about 16,900) are lower than in 2025 (about 19,000) and 2024 (about 18,800).
- **Week-to-week changes after the peak:** usually -0.5 to -2.3 points per week. Small upticks happen, for example 2025-11-08.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I did not find any Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market, or any published expert forecast, on NREVSS RV/EV positivity. CDC does not publish forecasts for RV/EV.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Weekly NREVSS updates, usually on Fridays: postings around 9/18, 9/25, 10/2, 10/9, 10/16 and 10/23 will show when the 2026 peak arrives and how high it gets. The deciding week (ending 10/24) will be posted on 10/30.
- Revisions: each weekly posting can revise recent weeks as late lab reports come in. The question resolves on the 10/30 version.
- Composition effects: rising testing for RSV, flu and COVID in October increases the number of tests (the denominator). In past years this coincided with RV/EV positivity drifting down. Timing of fall holidays such as Columbus Day and fall breaks could cause small blips.
- A possible enterovirus D68 or other enterovirus outbreak in fall 2026 could push positivity above the usual range. I found no reports of one as of 2026-09-14, but I did not search for this specifically.
